messages:
Jordan: FYI observed customers reporting unexpected charges when router does a midstream model fallback + client abort. looks like both model variants get provisional credits.
Priya: that's bad. fallback should only provision destination, not leave a dangling provisional for source. any traces?
Jordan: pasted a sanitized trace: 
```
2026-03-20T09:01:10Z INFO router: selected model=redwood-large-v1 dispatch_id=disp-9 token_est=300
2026-03-20T09:01:11Z INFO serving: dispatched batch->pool-a dispatch_id=disp-9 provisional_credit=300
2026-03-20T09:01:12Z INFO router: fallback triggered -> model=redwood-medium-v2 dispatch_id=disp-10 token_est=180
2026-03-20T09:01:12Z INFO serving: dispatched batch->pool-b dispatch_id=disp-10 provisional_credit=180
2026-03-20T09:01:12Z INFO stream: client aborted truncated_at=95 dispatch_id=disp-10
2026-03-20T09:01:13Z INFO toolcall: external-sentiment tokens=12 session=sess-77
2026-03-20T09:01:13Z INFO accounting: confirm provisional dispatch_id=disp-9 tokens=300
2026-03-20T09:01:14Z INFO accounting: confirm provisional dispatch_id=disp-10 tokens=180
2026-03-20T09:01:14Z INFO accounting: confirm toolcall tokens=12
```
Jordan: billing shows sum(300,180,12) even though only ~95 tokens reached the client and the final model dispatch was partly unused.
Leo: ugh, why did we confirm both dispatches? We should have a transfer semantics: when we fallback we should mark the earlier dispatch as superseded and attempt revoke.
Casey: we intentionally didn't revoke dispatch credits on fallback because of complexity with cross-pool handoffs and to avoid negative balance races. but clearly this produces overcharging in aborted flows.
Priya: what about conservative alternative: on fallback, tag the earlier provisional as superseded and only finalize the last dispatch on final ack; if final ack never arrives, reconcile via billing-window. that avoids double confirms.
Leo: that still leaves toolcall double-count: toolcalls are confirmed separately. if toolcall output never made it to client (e.g., truncated before toolcall result emitted), we should not bill. need host-level confirm after chunk delivered.
Jordan: agreed. proposed plan: 
1) router emits 'supersede' event for previous dispatch_id when fallback happens; accounting marks superseded provisional as pending_reclaim.
2) streaming service emits 'deliver-confirm' when tokens+toolcall outputs are flushed to client; accounting only confirms for deliver-confirmed tokens.
3) billing-window job finalizes pending_reclaim after T_grace (default 45s) and issues auto-refund if not confirmed.
Casey: sounds workable. main risk: increased tail latency for confirm path and more complexity in accounting state machine. but safer for customers.
Priya: console work: show dispatch lineage for a session with dispatch_ids and their state (provisional / superseded / confirmed / refunded). ops can run filters to find refunded sessions.
Leo: also need a metrics signal: rate of supersede->confirm mismatches so SREs can spot regressions post-rollout.
Jordan: action items:
- Casey: sketch accounting state transitions + invariants (due +2 days)
- Priya: console mock showing dispatch lineage and refund marker (due +4 days)
- Leo: add metric + alert for supersede-confirm delta (due +3 days)
- Jordan: implement deliver-confirm hook in streaming service (POC, due +5 days)

billing-bot: Created RED-1248: "midstream-fallback provisional double-credit" assigned to Casey, priority=high
Priya: thanks. marking this as P0 for next sprint planning. if anyone finds additional traces drop them here. :mag:
